summary.headline: Solara Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% QoQ to INR 392 crores and EBITDA rose 65% QoQ to INR 61 crores, led by the base business.
summary.overview: Management reported the highest revenue, gross margin and EBITDA in eight quarters, with revenue up 12% QoQ to INR 392 crores and EBITDA up 65% QoQ to INR 61 crores on flat operating costs. The base business, at about 26% EBITDA margin and 54% gross margin, drove the quarter, while ibuprofen continued to post negative EBITDA. The Board has appointed bankers to evaluate strategic options for ibuprofen, with a conclusion expected in H1 FY27, and the polymers carve-out from CRAMS is on hold. Debt was cut by about INR 158 crores in FY26 to a line of sight of about INR 503 crores by end-May 2026, and management has an internal target of being debt-free by FY29. No FY27/FY28 numerical outlook was given.

financial_highlights.change: INR 113 crores from first rights call money, INR 45 crores from operating cash flow

financial_highlights.metric: Expected debt after second call money

segments.name: Base business (developed markets, catalogue generics, polymer APIs)
segments.commentary: Operates at about 26% EBITDA margin and 54% gross margin per management, and accounts for about 75% of sales. Management cited a healthy order book and about 70% capacity utilisation, leaving about 30% spare.

segments.name: Ibuprofen
segments.commentary: Continues to generate negative EBITDA, which management said is eating into group EBITDA. Bankers are evaluating options (sale to a better owner as priority one, otherwise convert to a multiproduct facility), with conclusion expected in H1 FY27.

segments.name: CRAMS (incl. polymers carve-out)
segments.commentary: Management called CRAMS subscale, with annual revenue of about INR 10-12 crores; the combined CRAMS plus polymers figure is about INR 100 crores. The polymers carve-out under Synthix is on hold, and no CRAMS growth is being factored in.

segments.name: Derivatives
segments.commentary: Described as profitable and to continue as-is; largely dependent on captive ibuprofen supply, which a buyer or third-party sourcing would need to cover.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA outlook; management said it will not give one and hopes to repeat Q4 performance.
Base business EBITDA margin expected to stay around 25% plus or minus, per CFO, for the next few quarters.
Internal target of becoming debt-free (including working capital debt) by FY29.
Four to five DMF filings planned each year from FY26; meaningful revenue and margin impact expected around FY29-FY30.
Ibuprofen strategic options and Vizag roadmap to be clarified in H1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation about 70%, leaving about 30% spare capacity in existing facilities, mainly ex-ibuprofen sites; management said full 100% use is not realistic.
Debottlenecking projects (cycle-time improvements, not greenfield or brownfield) have started to add capacity for high-margin products.
No greenfield projects or big capex planned; only incremental capex.
Vizag plant was commissioned in 2024 but has been mothballed since then; the decision to move ibuprofen there or repurpose it awaits the H1 FY27 review.
Mysore site (30 acres, about 5 acres used) continues as an intermediate manufacturing site for the Mangalore product chain.
demand_pricing: Management attributed growth to new customers and new geographies for existing base products, and to higher share of wallet; no one-off spot orders or pre-buying was cited.

Ibuprofen global pricing upticks linked to the Middle East crisis were not reflected in Q4 because the order book was already priced; a possible tactical Q1 FY27 benefit was flagged but not confirmed.
Solara sources IBAP/IBB from third parties and is not backward integrated in ibuprofen; management said it lacks access to newer technologies used by competitors.
Around 70 products commercialised; top 15-20 products make up about 75% of business, with no single molecule dominant.
In polymers, management claimed about 50%-plus share of the market for a complex chemical, and said most other products are catalogue generics without tracked share.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 improvement structural or driven by one-offs such as restocking, spot orders or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Sandeep Rao said there were no one-offs; the growth came from the base business and its order book and utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the spare capacity and incremental margin potential of the base business?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% utilisation with roughly 30% spare capacity; debottlenecking added some capacity for high-margin products without big capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why are ibuprofen price improvements not visible in Q4 numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Sarat Kumar said Q4 order book was already secured at agreed prices, so Q1 FY27 may see a tactical benefit, too early to size.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for the Vizag plant?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Vizag was commissioned in 2024, mothballed since, and a decision on moving ibuprofen there or repurposing it awaits the H1 FY27 review.

qa_highlights.question: What are the strategic options for ibuprofen and what changed since last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Sale to a qualified buyer is option one, with converting to a multiproduct facility as option two; bankers were appointed and conclusion is expected in H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise more capital or stay debt-free?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said no further equity or debt raise is planned after the rights issue; internal target is debt-free by FY29, including working capital.

risks_watch: Ibuprofen remains loss-making; the strategic outcome (sale, conversion or wind-down) and its effect on the derivatives business and captive supply are unresolved.
Vizag fixed costs of INR 12-15 crores a year continue while the plant is mothballed.
Only about 30% spare capacity in existing sites limits growth without new capex, and the growth plan relies on debottlenecking and new DMFs that only pay off from FY29-FY30.
Management said the Middle East crisis is affecting global business, though it did not quantify the impact.
Debt reduction depends on the second rights call money being used by end-May 2026; the balance-sheet target is FY29.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the base business and Q4 momentum, but evasive on ibuprofen, Vizag and forward numbers, repeatedly deferring to H1 FY27 and declining to give outlook.
key_quotes: Our business has delivered the highest revenue, gross margins and EBITDA in the previous 8 quarters.
The primary driver of the strong performance has been undeniably our base business, which continues to gain momentum.
We want to keep our opex base minimal, and we have to increase year-on-year.
We have an internal target of making Solara debt-free by FY '29.

growth.why: No numerical FY27/FY28 revenue guidance; management only hopes to repeat Q4 (revenue +12% QoQ), with no greenfield or big capex, ~30% spare capacity at ~70% utilisation, and debottlenecking as the only capacity lever, so growth backing is vague.
